title: Keep the 10 p^2 row margin through a Schur complement (no new κ)
body:
## Question

#4462 transferred the exponents 11, 24, 26, 26 and 6 to the banded reference, with robust inverse bound `10 p^2`. Its open question is whether those exponents survive a Schur complement. The named first step is to restate the elimination gap with `10 p^2` in place of `16 p^2 - 1`.

## Result

Suppose the diagonal is 1 and every row and column has absolute off-sum at most `1 - 1/(10 p^2)`. One elimination step preserves a margin of at least `1/(10 p^2)` and does not increase an absolute row or column sum. After any principal elimination,

```text
||S^{-1}||_1 ≤ 10 p^2,    ||S^{-1}||_∞ ≤ 10 p^2,    ||S||_2 < 2.
```

The #4452 polynomial then has error below `p^6 exp(-p^2)`, bandwidth below `p^{26}`, and the same agreement distance. The five exponents apply to `S`. At `p = 2`, `(10 p^2)^2 = 1600 < 2048`, while `(16 p^2 - 1)^2 = 3969 > 2048`, so the older ceiling does not give spectral endpoint 11.

#4462's stronger margin `(4p-1)/(32 p^3)` is at least `1/(10 p^2)`, so those matrices meet the hypothesis. This package does not reprove that margin, the ideal gaps, or the core side 400.

**Claim type:** elimination lemma for one row-dominance margin. **No new κ.**

## Test plan

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-schur-gap
```

`PASS_GAUSSIAN_SCHUR_GAP` and `outcome=completed` on this machine. Maintainer replay has not been run.

Base `2a13eb1827784206202db90e5dc8327cf8a250db`, priority revision 7, selection refresh κ = `23/10000`.

Prepared by James Reed with substantial Cursor Grok 4.7 assistance.
